sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: springsteenlyrics.com, jungleland.it, brucespringsteen.it and Brucebase: after a press only the table view shows (springsteenlyrics.com keeps its navbar and breadcrumb, Brucebase its header and side bar); the rest of the site's page hides, and on a Brucebase event, song, venue, person, release, story or tag page so does the folded "Brucebase page". The switch (☰ SAED → View → "📄 Show the original page", Ctrl+M P, "▦ Back to the tables") shows the page as it was before the press, drawn by the site's own stylesheet in a frame over the page, with a note on top: links work and open in the tab, the site's own buttons may not (Brucebase's letter tabs do switch); Ctrl+M P works inside it too. On a Brucebase detail page the original view is the live wiki page instead: our tables hide, the wiki's title and page come back unfolded, everything on them works, and its own headings are no longer folded by us. A link followed on the copy asks first, as one on the page does ("You are about to leave this page").

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On a phone or tablet, the corner grip of a detail window (the one opened on a link) takes the finger more reliably: a drag on it could be taken for a scroll of the window's content and do nothing, depending on what lay under the window.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: setlist.fm: on a page long enough to scroll, the toolbar above our table (the action button and ☰ SAED) no longer disappears under a dark bar as soon as it sticks to the top. The backdrop meant to sit behind it lay over our whole section, in the colour of setlist.fm's dark page. Discogs and archive.org use the same rule now; MusicBrainz and the Springsteen sites are unchanged.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: discogs.com, archive.org and setlist.fm: after a press only the table view shows; the site's own page no longer sits under our tables. The switch of WIP.1 (☰ SAED → View → "📄 Show the original page", Ctrl+M P, "▦ Back to the tables") shows the site's own page again, live and fully working, with a "Live" note on top, and hides our section; back again, the tables are as you left them. The site's header stays only where it sits above our section (a Discogs master, release, artist or label page); where our section comes first (archive.org, setlist.fm, Discogs' search, submissions and user pages) the header hides with the page, and so does the footer. Before a press nothing changes. The site's page is shown as the site drew it: its own headings are not folded by us (archive.org's player and pictures are there after the switch); only Discogs' section headings keep their fold toggles.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: MusicBrainz pages: switch between the tables and the original page, and back, as often as you like, without a reload. After a "Show all …" press, ☰ SAED → View → "📄 Show the original page" (or Ctrl+M, then P) shows the page as it was just before the press: MusicBrainz's own list with its pages, its tracklist, its sidebar. A "▦ Back to the tables" button bottom right (or Ctrl+M P again) brings the tables back as you left them: the same rows, the filter you typed, the sort, and where you had scrolled. The original page is a copy taken at the press, so it switches at once and costs no request; a note on it says so, since MusicBrainz's own buttons in it (rating stars, "Load all tracks", the credits toggle) may not respond. Esc never switches. A load from disk takes the copy too. Every render opens on the tables; the choice is not remembered. With majkinetor's scripts, the button stacks with his corner launchers, and while the original page shows his launchers, keys and player behave as on a page without our tables. Like Event Horizon's V (org/majkinetor.org, "Switch between SAED's view and the original page (EH's V)"; approved mockup https://claude.ai/artifact/9wsKwn3kSr7LvhBkJVcijf).
